front: What are the regulation dimensions and end zone size for the field of play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 1 – Definitions and Markings
back: The field of play shall be 110 yards (100 metres) long by 65 yards (60 metres) wide, with an end zone 20 yards (18.28 metres) long at each end.

front: How are the end zone, goal line, and field of play areas defined in relation to their bounding lines? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 1 – Definitions and Markings
back: End Zone: bounded by the goal line, end zone sidelines, and dead line; the goal line is part of the end zone. Field of Play: bounded by the goal lines and the sidelines.

front: What specifically makes something out of bounds along the field boundaries? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 2 – Boundaries
back: The bounds are defined as the inside of the sidelines, end zone sidelines, and dead lines, and these boundary lines are out of bounds.

front: From what exact edge are all field measurements to be taken? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 3 – Field Dimension Measurements
back: All measurements shall be taken from the inside edge of any boundary line.

front: How must the field be marked in 5-yard increments across the width, and how far do these lines extend? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 4 – Distance Lines
back: The field of play shall be marked every 5 yards (metres) by lines parallel to the goal line, extending completely across the field between the sidelines.

front: Which yard lines must be specially marked, and how are they marked? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 5 – Special Lines
back: The 35 and 45 yard (30 and 40 metre) lines shall be of double thickness or double lines.

front: Where are hash marks placed relative to the sidelines, and what is the pattern of marking on each 5-yard stripe? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 6 – Hash Marks
back: Twenty-four yards (22 metres) from each sideline, each 5 yard (metre) stripe is marked by a short cross stripe parallel to the sideline (hash marks).

front: What marker requirements apply at the intersections of the goal lines/sidelines and the dead line/end zone sidelines? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 8 – End Zone Markings
back: The four intersections of the goal lines and sidelines, and the four intersections of the dead line and the end zone sidelines, shall be marked only by flexible markers placed at the intersection and are considered inbounds; no rigid or wooden object may be used, and if rigid objects are present they must be removed before the start of the game.

front: What are the required physical characteristics and acceptable colors for the flexible end zone marker pylons? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 8 – End Zone Markings
back: They must be soft, flexible, four-sided pylons, 4” x 4” (10 cm x 10 cm) with an overall height of 18 inches (46 cm) (which may include a two inch (5 cm) space between the bottom of the pylon and the ground), and be orange or red in colour.

front: What are the required goal post spacing and crossbar height above the ground? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: The goal post assembly consists of 2 vertical goal posts 18 feet 6 inches (5.64 metres) apart, centred on the goal line, with a crossbar whose upper edge is 10 feet (3.05 metres) above the ground.

front: How high must goal posts be above ground level, and how does a new installation differ from existing installations? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: For safety reasons, goal posts must be at least 20 feet (6.1 metres) above the ground level; for new installations, goal posts should measure 30 ft (9.1 metres) above ground level.

front: What padding and responsibility requirements apply to goal posts? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 9 – Goal Post Assembly
back: All goal posts must be properly padded with goal post pads meeting manufacturer’s specifications; it is the responsibility of the home team to provide the padding, and on a neutral field the participating teams decide which team is responsible.

front: What boundary adjustments must be made if the field is smaller than regulation due to tracks or obstructions? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 10 – Non-Regulation Fields
back: When the length or width is less than regulation, a clear set of boundary lines shall be provided at least 1 foot (0.3 metres) inside the track or obstruction.

front: What actions count as a “play” for rule application? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 1: The Field | Article 11 – Play
back: A play is defined as any legally run scrimmage play (run, pass, kick), a convert attempt, or a kick-off during both regulation time and overtime.

front: What are the required construction and inflation limits for the four-panel ball (pressure range, material, and shape)? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 2: The Ball | Article 1 – Description
back: The ball is a four-panel ball made of pebbled grain leather, enclosing a rubber bladder, tightly inflated to not less than 12 1/2 lbs (85 kPa) and not more than 13 1/2 lbs (95 kPa). It shall be in the shape of a prolate spheroid.

front: What are the specified size and weight ranges for the ball’s long axis, short axis, and overall weight? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 2: The Ball | Article 1 – Description
back: Long axis circumference: 27 3/4 to 28 1/2 inches (700 to 725 mm). Short axis circumference: 20 3/4 to 21 3/8 inches (525 to 540 mm). Long axis length: 10 7/8 to 11 7/16 inches (275 to 290 mm). Weight: 14 to 15 ounces (400 to 425 grams).

front: Under what condition does the referee decide whether the ball is suitable, and who provides the ball? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 2: The Ball | Article 1 – Description
back: The Home Team shall provide a league approved ball or balls. The decision of the Referee shall be final as to the suitability of the ball.

front: How must the ball’s color differ for day games vs. night games, and what uniform-color restriction applies in both? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 2: The Ball | Article 2 – Day and Night Games
back: For day games, the ball shall be of a natural tan colour. For night games, the ball must be of such colour as will make it clearly visible. In both day and night games, the colour of the ball shall, in no way, closely blend with the colour of the uniforms of the competing teams.

front: On wet days, how many balls are recommended and who is suggested to help keep them clean and dry? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 2: The Ball | Article 3 – Wet Day Procedure
back: On wet days, it is recommended that at least three balls be available which may be changed at the discretion of the Referee. It is suggested that “ball persons” be used, one on either side of the field, to keep the balls as clean and dry as possible.

front: How many minutes of actual playing time are there in the game at (a) general level and (b) High School level or equivalent and below? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 3: The Game | Article 1 – Length of Game
back: (a) 60 minutes actual playing time, divided into 4 periods of 15 minutes each. (b) 48 minutes actual playing time, divided into 4 periods of 12 minutes each.

front: At the start of the game, who makes the initial choice among kicking off, receiving the kick off, or defending an end of the field—and what changes at the start of the 3rd period? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 3: The Game | Article 2 – Choice of Kick Off, Receiving Kick Off, or End of Field
back: At the start of the game, the visiting team captain or the team winning the coin toss declares whether to have first choice at the start of the 1st or 2nd half. The captain with first choice for the 1st half chooses one of: (1) Kicking Off (2) Receiving the kick off (3) Defending an end of the field. The other captain chooses among the remaining 2 (or 1) options. At the start of the 3rd period, the procedure is reversed.

front: How is play put into play at the start of the 2nd and 4th periods after teams change ends? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 3: The Game | Article 3 – Change of End
back: At the end of the 1st and 3rd periods, teams change ends. At the start of the 2nd and 4th periods, the ball is put into play by the team entitled to do so at a point corresponding exactly to where the ball became dead at the opposite end of the field, and in exactly the same manner as if play had not been interrupted by the end of the previous period.

front: How long is the rest period at halftime? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 3: The Game | Article 4 – Half Time
back: At the end of the 2nd period, a 20-minute rest period is allowed (or such other rest period as the league shall decide).

front: What penalty applies if a team is late appearing on the field at the start of the 1st or 3rd period? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 3: The Game | Article 5 – Late Start
back: Penalty – L10. No option.

front: When the score is tied at the end of the 4th period, what happens if no written tie-breaking regulations have been prepared? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 3: The Game | Article 6 – Tie Game
back: Officials instruct both teams to retire to their respective team areas, then review the tie-breaking procedure at center field. Captains are escorted to center field for a coin toss; the winner chooses (1) Offense or defense with offense at the opponent’s 35-yard line to start, or (2) which end of the field is used for the overtime period. The loser takes the remaining option for the first extra period and has the first choice for the two options in subsequent even-numbered extra periods. Extra periods: each team puts the ball in play by a snap on or between the hash marks of the opponent’s 35-yard line, and each team retains the ball until it scores or fails to make a first down (ball remains alive after a change of team possession until declared dead). The team scoring more points in an extra period wins; if still tied after three extra periods, any subsequent touchdown must be followed by a two-point conversion. There are no team time-outs during overtime play.

front: How many players from each team are on the field at any one time? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 4: Teams | Article 1 – Teams
back: Each team consists of 12 players on the field at any one time.

front: Which team is identified as Team A and which as Team B? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 4: Teams | Article 2 – Team Designation
back: The team which puts the ball into play is identified as Team A, and the other team is identified as Team B (for identification in Approved Rulings in the Case Book).

front: Who is the sole communicator between a team and the officials, and what is their role regarding rule explanations? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: Each team must have on the field a player designated as captain. The captain is the sole communicator between the team and the officials (through the Referee) and is entitled to an explanation of the rules.

front: What penalty applies if a player (or anyone on the bench) comments to benefit the officials, and is there an option? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: Commenting by a player, or any occupant of the bench, for the supposed benefit of the officials shall be penalized: Penalty L10. No option.

front: Under what situations will the referee inform the captain when a choice must be made? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 4: Teams | Article 3 – Team Captains
back: The referee will inform a captain when a choice is to be made, such as: on a kick off at the start of a half; after a touchdown or field goal; or in the case of a foul where the captain of the non-offending team is given the choice of the penalty, or option provided.

front: When does the game clock start on the referee’s signal (list the conditions)? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 5: Timing | Article 1 – Time Starts
back: Time shall start on the signal of the Referee when: (a) after a kickoff the ball touches/touched by a player of either team in bounds; (b) the ball is ready to be scrimmaged; (c) the ball is snapped after a “time count” foul, or after a timeout due to the noise of the crowd; (d) the ball is snapped following a requested time out; (e) the ball is snapped following an incomplete forward pass, or the ball being carried out of bounds, after the 3 minute warning signal in any half; (f) the ball is snapped immediately following a play where possession changes after the 3 minute warning in any half (including change after a score of 1 or 3 points when put into play by scrimmage); (g) the ball is snapped on a play immediately following a kickoff/kick from scrimmage/return kick/open field kick after the 3 minute warning in any half; (h) the ball is snapped after penalty application for a foul that occurs after the 3 minute warning in any half (non-offending team may decline the penalty and permit time to resume as though no foul occurred); (i) following a time out or after the 3 minute warning, when the game clock is held from the previous play and play is stopped for a procedural penalty by either team—the game clock shall be held until the snap whether yardage is accepted or not.

front: When does time stop on the signal of a field official (list the conditions)? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 5: Timing | Article 2 – Time Stops
back: Time shall stop on the signal of a field official when: (a) a score has been made and throughout any convert attempt; (b) a live ball goes out of bounds; (c) a forward pass is incomplete; (d) penalty application is required; (e) three or more players from either team substitute at the same time; (f) player injury occurs (time stops after the ball is dead and the injured player must be replaced); (g) time expires at the end of a period; (h) the ball becomes dead after the three-minute warning signal in any half; (i) any field official recognizes a request for a time out; (j) the referee suspends play (defective equipment, measurements, etc.); (k) a play ends in which Team B has gained possession at some point during the play; (l) termination of all kick plays occurs.

front: If the ball becomes dead with only a short time remaining in a period, what advantage does the possession team get? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 5: Timing | Article 3 – End of Period
back: If in any period, the ball becomes dead with only a short period of time remaining, the team in possession is entitled to one complete play even though that play may extend beyond the normal termination of that period.

front: Under the mercy rule, when does the clock run running time, and what exceptions prevent stopping? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 5: Timing | Article 5 – Mercy Rule
back: Any time after the first half, if the difference in score becomes 35 points or more, the clock will be running time for the remainder of the game, except for injuries, scores, timeouts, or any reason the referee deems necessary to stop the clock. When the clock has been stopped, it will re-start based on rule 1-5-1. (Note: mercy rule does not apply for U Sport and CJFL levels.)

front: When is a player considered to be in possession of the ball? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 1 – Player Possession
back: A player is in possession of the ball when it is firmly held in the hand(s), arm(s), leg(s), or under the body.

front: In a disputed situation where players of opposite teams have possession, who is awarded possession? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 2 – Disputed Possession
back: It belongs to the player who first gained possession and has not lost possession.

front: If players of opposite teams legally gain simultaneous possession, how is possession awarded? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 3 – Simultaneous Possession
back: It belongs to the team which last previously had possession.

front: When a forward pass is caught simultaneously by eligible receivers of both teams, which team is awarded the ball (per the rule cross-reference)? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 3 – Simultaneous Possession
back: The ball shall belong to Team A (Rule 6-4-6-c).

front: On a kickoff legally caught simultaneously by players of opposite teams, how is possession determined based on whether it was touched before the simultaneous catch? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 3 – Simultaneous Possession
back: If caught simultaneously before it has been touched by any other player after the kickoff, the kickoff is repeated at the previous line of kick off. If it has been legally touched by another player (or players), possession goes to the team which last touched it before the simultaneous possession.

front: Under a scrimmage play, when does possession stay with Team A vs. switch to Team B? What is the ball called if neither team has it? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team A is in possession until it loses possession (e.g., fumble, blocked kick). Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team A or Team B gains possession, the ball is in neither team’s possession and is a “loose ball.”

front: On a forward pass, when does possession remain with Team A and when does it change to Team B? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team A is in possession until the pass is ruled incomplete or the ball is intercepted by Team B. Team B is in possession when a B player intercepts the pass.

front: For a scrimmage kick, when does possession belong to Team A, when does it belong to Team B, and what is the ball called while neither team has possession? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team A is in possession until the ball is kicked. Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team B or Team A gains possession, the ball is in neither team’s possession and is a “ball in flight.”

front: For a return kick, when does Team B have possession and what happens to the ball between kicks and regaining possession? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Team B is in possession until the B player has kicked the ball, which is then “in flight” until either Team A or Team B regains possession.

front: For the kickoff, who has possession before the kick, and how is possession determined afterward before either team regains it? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession
back: Neither team is in possession prior to the kick off. Team B is in possession when a B player gains possession. Until Team B or Team A gains possession, the ball is in neither team’s possession and is a “ball in flight.”

front: What special possession/timing provision applies when a kicked ball other than a kickoff is legally touched by a player? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 6: Possession | Article 4 – Change of Possession (Note)
back: If a kicked ball other than a kickoff is legally touched by a player of either team, such touching shall be deemed to be possession when penalty applications are involved with before change of possession, loose ball, ball in flight, or after change of possession.

front: When is the ball considered “in play” from the moment it’s put into action? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: The ball is in play from when it has been put into play by a kick off or scrimmage until a field official stops play by sounding the whistle.

front: Does the ball remain in play if it strikes an official or goes loose? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: Yes. The ball is in play if it strikes an official who is not out of bounds (except on a forward pass), if it is on the ground not in possession of a player, and if an offside pass is made and/or the ball goes loose.

front: Under what goal-post or end-zone contact situations is the ball in play? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 1 – Ball in Play
back: The ball is in play if a dribbled ball hits the goal post assembly; a kicked ball hits the goal post assembly after striking the ground, a player, or official, or after being kicked from the end zone; or a lateral pass hits the goal post assembly.

front: When may play be stopped for a player injury or to impose a penalty? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 2 – Injury Stoppage
back: Play shall not be stopped because of player injury, or to impose a penalty, until the ball is dead.

front: How is delay handled for player injury, and what is the penalty for unauthorized delay? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 2 – Injury Stoppage
back: No delay shall be allowed for player injury, or for any other reason, except by permission of a field official. Unauthorized delay is penalized: L10, no option.

front: What happens if medical attention is needed due to injury or equipment related to bleeding? Rule 1 | Section 7: Live Ball | Article 2 – Injury Stoppage
back: To avoid penalizing teams unduly, the Referee will call an official time out of no more than two (2) minutes for medical attention and/or care of equipment related to bleeding; neither team is charged with a time out.

front: When does the ball become dead under these circumstances? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: The ball becomes dead when: (a) a field official blows the whistle to end play; (b) the ball or a player with possession goes out of bounds; (c) any score is made; (d) the ball carrier is tackled/held and forward progress is halted; (e) a forward pass is declared incomplete or strikes a game official/goal post assembly/downs box marker/distance chain rod; (f) it is in possession of a player lying on the ground or is being held for a kick off prior to the kick off; (g) it strikes the opponent’s goal post assembly in flight from a punt/return kick/place kick/kick off without touching the ground, a player, or an official after being kicked (with the specified field-goal/convert allowance); (h) any part of a ball carrier other than hands or feet touches the ground, with the ball dead at the point held when it touched (exception for field goal/convert hold); (i) the ball carrier falls on a player on the ground (except in the close line play area); (j) immediately when the ball carrier loses their helmet; (k) when a ball carrier begins, simulates, or fakes a foot-first slide.

front: What is the exception to the dead-ball rule when the ball carrier touches the ground with something other than hands or feet? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1
back: The ball is not dead when a player is holding the ball for a field goal or convert attempt.

front: If the whistle is blown inadvertently while a team is in possession, what choices does that team have? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 8: Dead Ball | Article 1 (Note 4)
back: With a team in possession, the team in possession may choose to: (i) cancel the current play and repeat it where it began (PLS or kick-off), or (ii) have the play terminate at the PBH when the whistle was blown (downs continue if distance not gained). Note: If the whistle is blown inadvertently while the ball is in the air on a pass play, the play is repeated from PLS with no option.

front: When is the ball considered to be in the End Zone? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 9: End Zone | Article 1 – Definition
back: The ball is in the End Zone when any part of the ball is on, or behind the goal line (even in the air), or when any part of the ball touches the plane of the goal line.

front: Under what condition is the ball NOT in the End Zone? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 9: End Zone | Article 1 – Definition
back: The ball is not in the End Zone when the whole ball is completely ahead of the goal line, or the plane of the goal line.

front: When is the ball considered out of bounds? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 1 – Definition
back: The ball is out of bounds when it touches any boundary line, the ground, or any object on or beyond these lines (including an official, any player, or substitute).

front: Under what condition can a ball carrier touch beyond the boundary without the ball becoming out of bounds? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 1 – Definition
back: If the player in possession touches any boundary line, the ground, or any object beyond these lines except a field official or another player who is out of bounds, while the ball carrier is fully in bounds.

front: Where does the ball belong when it is carried out of bounds on the field of play (and what exception applies on third down)? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 2 – Carried Out of Bounds
back: It belongs to the team carrying it out of bounds at the point where the ball crossed the line before going out of bounds, except on third down when the required distance has not been gained.

front: Which team gets possession when the ball is kicked out of bounds on the field of play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 3 – Kicked Out of Bounds
back: The opposite team gets possession, subject to the option of penalty applicable on the play.

front: What points can result when a player kicks a ball out of bounds in their own end zone? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 3 – Kicked Out of Bounds
back: It results in a score of 1 or 2 points, unless the ball is in the end zone from a forward pass intercepted in the end zone, or as a result of a fumble into the end zone by an opponent.

front: When does a forward pass thrown out of bounds remain with the passing team? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 4 – Forward Pass Thrown Out of Bounds
back: It shall remain in possession of the passing team, except on third down when the required distance has not been gained.

front: With the listed exceptions, which team gets the ball after a fumble out of bounds or after a ball touched by a player on the field goes out of bounds, and where is it placed? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 5 – Last Touched
back: It belongs to the team which last touched the ball at 24 yards (22 metres) in from the sideline at whichever point is closer to the goal line of the team entitled to possession—either at the point where the ball went out of bounds or where the ball was last touched in the field of play.

front: When a player fumbles directly over the opponent’s goal line and then out of bounds in the end zone without the ball touching an opponent, how is it ruled? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 6 – Into End Zone
back: Ruled as a fumble, out of bounds, in the field of play; the ball is declared dead at the point where it was last touched in the field of play.

front: What happens when a player fumbles over the opponent’s goal line and it is last touched by a teammate without gaining possession, then goes out of bounds in the end zone? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 6 – Into End Zone
back: The ball is awarded to the team making the fumble, at the point of the original fumble.

front: When is there no score and the ball awarded to the opponent after a fumble over the opponent’s goal line goes out of bounds in the end zone? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 6 – Into End Zone
back: When the fumble is recovered by an opponent, or it is last touched by an opponent without gaining possession, and then goes out of bounds in the end zone—there is no score and the ball is awarded to the opponent at any point on or between the hash marks on the 20 yard (20 metre) line if the ball goes dead in the end zone.

front: If a player fumbles or directs the ball from the field of play into their own end zone and it goes out of bounds without possession being gained by either team, what is awarded? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 6 – Into End Zone
back: A safety touch shall be awarded.

front: What score is awarded when a player fumbles the ball in their own end zone out of bounds in the end zone? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 7 – From End Zone
back: A score of 1 or 2 points shall be awarded as applicable (with the stated exceptions noted in Note 1).

front: How is it ruled when a player fumbles from their own end zone over the goal line and then out of bounds without the ball touching an opponent? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 7 – From End Zone
back: It is ruled as an offside pass in the end zone.

front: In the offside pass in the end zone scenario, what options/penalties are given to Team A and Team B? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 7 – From End Zone
back: Penalty: Team A – 1.2 D safety touch to B, or B option to allow A to scrimmage 24 yards (22 metres) in from the out-of-bounds point, downs continue; or 3D safety touch to B, or B possession 24 yards (22 metres) in from out-of-bounds point. Team B – 1 or 2 points as applicable, or A option to allow B to scrimmage 24 yards (22 metres) in from the out-of-bounds point.

front: What exceptions prevent a score in Article 7 (a) or (b)? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 7 – From End Zone
back: No score in (a) or (b) if the ball is in the end zone from a forward pass intercepted in the end zone, or as a result of a fumble into the end zone by an opponent, or if the ball carrier has been knocked back into the end zone by an opponent and is not subsequently free to advance the ball.

front: Under what conditions is it illegal for a player to go out of bounds and return to the field to participate in the play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 8 – Player Out of Bounds
back: It is illegal for a player to go out of bounds and return to the field and participate in the play unless the player went out of bounds as a result of: a) a slippery field, b) contact with an opponent, or c) a missed block or tackle.

front: What must an out-of-bounds player do to legally re-enter and participate? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 8 – Player Out of Bounds
back: The player is allowed to return but must re-establish themselves in the field of play with at least one foot in bounds and no contact with out of bounds.

front: What is the penalty if a player illegally participates by reaching back into or re-entering the field to touch/recover a loose ball? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 8 – Player Out of Bounds
back: Penalty – LB PF.

front: What is the penalty when a player illegally participates by going out of bounds on a Kick-off before possession has been legally gained? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 8 – Player Out of Bounds
back: Penalty - L10 from the point of kick-off: repeat kick-off or option.

front: What is the penalty when a player illegally participates by going out of bounds on a Kick-off after possession has been legally gained? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 8 – Player Out of Bounds
back: Penalty - L10 PP, PBH, PBD or option.

front: What happens if a player of Team B reaches back into the field of play while still out of bounds and touches a kickoff? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 10: Out of Bounds | Article 8 – Player Out of Bounds
back: The ball is dead at the spot of touch, with possession awarded along with a 10-yard penalty for Illegal participation.

front: What uniform or equipment requirements prevent injuries or interference with the opponent, and what action can the Referee take if violated? Rule 1 | Conduct of the Game | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1 – General
back: No player may wear equipment that may injure the opponent; the Referee may remove any player whose equipment, in the Referee’s opinion, endangers a participant. No team may wear uniforms that blend closely with the ball’s color, and numbers must be easy to identify.

front: Which equipment items are mandatory for all players, and what is a key restriction on knee protection (straps)? Rule 1 | Conduct of the Game | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1 – General
back: Mandatory equipment: (1) knee protection (soft padding fully captured in continuous material, or insertable in football pants); knee protection cannot include any strap featuring a buckle, Velcro, clip, or any strap that could become unfastened during play. (2) thigh guards, (3) hip pads with tailbone protector, (4) shoulder pads, (5) mouthguard (as specified in Article 3), (6) shoes meeting the specs or approved types as described, and (7) items 1,2,3,4 plus all back plates and rib protectors must be covered by pants or jersey (except certain snap-in soft foam hip/tail pad systems). (8) helmet and face guard per rule 1-11-2.

front: When a team uses illegal material or slippery substances, or illegal gloves, what consequence applies and when is the offending player removed? Rule 1 | Conduct of the Game | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1 – General
back: Adhesive material/grease or any slippery substance applied to a player’s person or clothing that affects the ball or an opponent is illegal. Any gloves with webbing between the digits are illegal. For both violations, the offending player is removed from the game until the illegal material/substance/gloves are removed; immediate substitution is made but the game is not delayed.

front: What are the uniform-number rules (including changes during the game), and what happens if a jersey is torn? Rule 1 | Conduct of the Game | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1 – General
back: All players’ numbers must conform to those listed on the score sheet, and players must retain the same numbers throughout the game except when the Referee gives permission to change. If a sweater is torn, the Referee shall allow reasonable time for substitution, but any change in number must be reported to the scorer.

front: What is the penalty if a player ties or knots team jerseys? Rule 1 | Conduct of the Game | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1 – General
back: It is illegal to tie or knot team jerseys. Penalty: the offending player shall be removed from the game until the illegal equipment is replaced or the score sheet is corrected.

front: What is the penalty when a player has a second mouthguard or an illegal extra mouthguard? Rule 1 | Conduct of the Game | Section 11 – Uniform & Equipment | Article 1 – General
back: It is illegal for a player to have a second mouthguard (including an extra-oral mouthguard attached or fixated to the helmet or facemask). Penalty: loss of 5 yards from the point where the ball would have been put into play (if no other foul had occurred), or added to the penalty for any other foul; the offending player is removed until the illegal equipment is replaced. Immediate substitution is made but the game is not delayed. If more than 1 player offends on the same play, only 1 L5 is applied for that play; subsequent plays are penalized the same way (L5 each play where 1 or more players offend).

front: What must happen if a player who is not registered by name and number appears before the start of the game? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 1 – Registration
back: The offending player shall be removed from the game until the score sheet has been corrected. Immediate substitution will be made, and the game shall not be delayed.

front: Is a score by a non-registered player automatically illegal? Under what condition? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 1 – Registration
back: Any score made by a non-registered player is legal, provided the player is then registered on the score sheet.

front: Under what condition may substitutes enter the field of play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: Substitutes may enter the field of play when the ball is dead and only at that time.

front: When may a team’s substitutes no longer enter the field, regardless of how many players are on the field? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: After Team A breaks its huddle, the sideline officials raise their arms to shoulder level; after that, no substitute shall enter the field for any reason.

front: What makes a “sleeper play” illegal? How is it defined? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: It is illegal to use substitution proceedings, or alleged substitution proceedings, to deceive the opponent. A “sleeper play” is defined as a pass play or kick play designed to deceive the opponent.

front: What is the penalty for Team A if substitution deception leads to an illegal sleeper play on the subsequent play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: Penalty: Team A 1.2D – L10 DR, 3D DG – L10 DR, 3D DNG – LB, PBD.

front: What requirement applies to a substitute who enters the field to the extent they can communicate with a teammate? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: The substitute must remain on the field for the subsequent play.

front: What is the penalty if a substitute does not remain on the field for the subsequent play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 2 – Substitution Procedure
back: Penalty: Team A 1.2D – L10 DR, 3D DG – L10 DR, 3D DNG – LB, PBD. Team B L10.

front: What is the maximum number of players and/or substitutes a team may have on the field during a play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 3 – Excess Number of Players
back: It is illegal for a team to have more than 12 players and/or substitutes on the field during a play.

front: What is the penalty for having an excess number of players on the field, and who is responsible for fielding the correct number? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 12: Players and Substitutes | Article 3 – Excess Number of Players
back: Penalty: Team A 1.2D – L10 DR, 3D DG – L10 DR, 3D DNG – LB, PBD. Team B L10. Note: Coaches, not officials, are responsible for fielding the correct number of players.

front: Who are the only persons legally allowed to occupy positions on the sidelines during the game? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: Field officials, the Downbox Official, the Yardstick Officials, the Time Keeper, and the Scorer.

front: What are the location limits and enclosure requirements for a team bench area relative to the sideline? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: The bench area must be a minimum of 5 yards (5 metres) and a maximum of 10 yards (10 metres) from the sideline. It must be enclosed by a line 4 inches (10 cm) wide located at least 2 yards (2 metres) minimum and 5 yards (5 metres) optimum from the sideline, and a line at each end of the bench 5 yards (5 metres) from the end. (See Field Drawing.)

front: What happens if a person occupies the sideline/bench area illegally (not staying within the enclosed area when play is in progress), and what is the penalty? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 1 – Sideline Privileges & Restrictions
back: Bench occupants must remain within the enclosed area except during legal substitution proceedings or by express permission of the Referee to keep the sideline clear. Penalty: L10, no option, from point where the ball would have been put in play if no foul had occurred.

front: When is a sideline conference between coaches and players of each team legal? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 2 – Time-Out Conferences
back: It is legal during an official time out, and also whenever the clock is stopped and a significant time delay occurs (e.g., a measurement, injury, TV commercial, etc.).

front: What is prohibited for an unauthorized person during play? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: An unauthorized person shall not enter or reach into the field while play is in progress and/or interfere with a player of either team or with a loose ball.

front: If an unauthorized person interferes acting to the advantage of the team in possession, what are the possible outcomes/penalties? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: Penalty: If it is obvious to the Referee that a score (such as a rouge or safety touch) would have been made, then the score will be awarded. If not, L10 PBH.

front: If an unauthorized person interferes acting to the advantage of the team not in possession, what determines whether a touchdown is awarded or what other enforcement occurs? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: Penalty: If it is obvious to the Referee that a touchdown would have been scored, or if the unauthorized person is a substitute/coach/trainer/other occupant of the team bench, a touchdown shall be awarded. If not, the non-offending team is awarded: (1) Half the distance to the goal line from PLS or PBD. (2) For illegal interference on a forward pass: if the infraction is on the field of play—half the distance to the goal line from PF; if in the end zone—against Team A, the ball at the 1 yard (1 metre) line (unless a touchdown is awarded); against Team B, the ball at the 20 yard (20 metre) line. (3) 3 downs, regardless of time remaining in the period (with stated exceptions).

front: What is the penalty if an unauthorized person touches or kicks a loose ball and would have prevented a score? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: Penalty: If it is obvious to the Referee that a score would have been made, the score will be awarded. If the person is a substitute/coach/trainer/other bench occupant, the team is penalized half the distance to their goal line from PF. If the non-offending team was previously in possession or was normally expecting to gain possession by receiving a scrimmage kick, the ball is awarded and 3 additional downs are given regardless of time remaining (with stated exceptions). If not associated as described, the play is repeated at PLS, subject to team penalties applied at PLS.

front: What is the consequence if the unauthorized person is a substitute, coach, trainer, or other occupant of the team bench? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 3 – Interference by Unauthorized Persons
back: Penalty: Disqualification from further participation in any capacity.

front: During a stoppage for injury, what may team personnel do once the Referee permits them to enter the field? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 5 – Injuries
back: With the Referee’s permission, personnel may enter the field to attend to the injured player or bring water to the players on the field. They may not undertake any coaching activities while on the field.

front: How long must a player leave the game after being stopped for injury or for equipment repair? Rule 1 – Conduct of the Game | Section 13: Non Players | Article 5 – Injuries
back: When play is stopped for a player injury, that player must leave the game for at least three plays; for equipment repair, the player must leave for at least one play.
